title: Stalk of a pro-etale sheaf at a geometric point
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme and $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the universes and small skeleton of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], with $\Omega$ in the chosen bound. A pointed neighbourhood is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ consisting of a weakly étale object $U\to Y$ [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] and a lift $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ of $\bar y$. A morphism $(U,\bar u)\to(U',\bar u')$ is a $Y$-morphism $h:U\to U'$ with $h\circ\bar u=\bar u'$. Denote this category, formed in the larger universe, by $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$.

For a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on this site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $D_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ send $(U,\bar u)$ to $\mathcal F(U)$ and the opposite of $h$ to the restriction $\mathcal F(h):\mathcal F(U')\to\mathcal F(U)$. Its stalk is the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]
$$
\mathcal F_{\bar y}=\varinjlim_{\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}}D_{\mathcal F}.
$$
Concretely, this is the disjoint union of the sets $\mathcal F(U)$ over pointed neighbourhoods, modulo the equivalence relation generated by $(U',\bar u',s)\sim(U,\bar u,\mathcal F(h)(s))$ for every pointed morphism $h$ and $s\in\mathcal F(U')$. The opposite index category is filtered; its nonempty, common-refinement and equalization conditions are verified in the steps below.

For a sheaf of modules over a fixed commutative ring $A$ (restriction maps $A$-linear), the same diagram is taken in $A$-modules. More generally, for a sheaf $\mathcal O$ of commutative rings and a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], first form the stalks of the underlying sets by this construction. Define addition, multiplication and the action of $\mathcal O_{\bar y}$ on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ by restricting finitely many representatives to a common pointed refinement and performing the corresponding operations there. This specifies the module stalk without requiring the semilinear restriction maps to be maps over one fixed section ring.

proof.text: The object $(Y,\bar y)$ is a pointed neighbourhood: the identity is flat and its diagonal is an identity under the canonical identification, hence it is weakly étale by definition. The specified size bound contains $Y$ and $\Omega$. Passing to the chosen skeleton transports this object and its lift along the representative isomorphism. Thus $\mathcal N_{\bar y}$ is nonempty.

proof.text: For $(U,\bar u)$ and $(V,\bar v)$, take $P=U\times_YV$. The projection $P\to U$ is the base change of $V\to Y$, so is weakly étale; composing with $U\to Y$ is weakly étale by the composition lemma. The fibre-product universal property gives the unique lift $(\bar u,\bar v):\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$, and both projections preserve it. These are a common refinement. The size convention allows this finite construction in the chosen bound and replacement by its skeleton representative.

source.place: Tag 0F6B, lemma-cofinal-etale, and the preceding definition of pro-etale neighbourhood; its proof refers to etale-cohomology.tex, lemma-cofinal-etale (Tag 03PQ)

proof.text: Let $h_1,h_2:(U,\bar u)\rightrightarrows(V,\bar v)$ be parallel pointed morphisms. The object $Q=V\times_YV$ is weakly étale over $Y$ by base change and composition. The $Y$-morphism $(h_1,h_2):U\to Q$ is therefore weakly étale by the between-objects lemma. Form $E=U\times_{Q}V$ using this morphism and $\Delta_{V/Y}:V\to Q$. Then $E\to V$ is weakly étale by base change, and $E\to Y$ by composition. The equality $h_1\bar u=\bar v=h_2\bar u$ gives a lift $(\bar u,\bar v)$ to $E$. If $p:E\to U$ and $q:E\to V$ are its projections, the pullback equation says $(h_1p,h_2p)=(q,q)$, hence $h_1p=h_2p$; $p$ is pointed. This is the needed equalizing refinement. Steps 1–3 give precisely the three defining conditions for $\mathcal N_{\bar y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ to be filtered. No separation, finite-presentation or quasi-compactness hypothesis has been used.

proof.text: The restriction maps form a diagram because a sheaf is a contravariant functor. The size convention supplies a small indexing category in the larger universe: a small skeleton of site objects together with the sets of their lifts has a set of objects and arrows. For sets, the quotient in the statement has its cocone maps $s\mapsto[U,\bar u,s]$. A compatible family of maps out of the sets $\mathcal F(U)$ descends uniquely to this quotient, since its values agree on each generating pair, proving the colimit universal property. For fixed $A$-modules, take $\bigoplus_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)$ and quotient by the submodule generated by $\iota_{U'}s-\iota_U\mathcal F(h)(s)$. A compatible family of linear maps extends uniquely to the direct sum and annihilates these generators, giving exactly the module colimit universal property. For varying $\mathcal O$, common refinements allow all operands to be represented at one object; two choices can be compared at a common refinement, with any different parallel arrows equalized by step 3. Relations generating equality can also be compared after finitely many such refinements. Ring and module identities hold after these restrictions because they hold in each $\mathcal O(U)$ and $\mathcal F(U)$, and restriction respects every operation by the definition of an $\mathcal O$-module sheaf. Thus the stated operations are well-defined.
